newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SOCCER-NORWAY FIND IT TOUGH AGAINST HUNGARIANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NORWAY FIND IT TOUGH AGAINST HUNGARIANS.

text.p: Hungary came close to causing an upset on Sunday when they outplayed Norway in the first half of a 1-1 draw in their World Cup European group three qualifier.
Fresh from their 4-2 win over Brazil last week, the Norwegians, eight of whom played in the English premier league this season, were expected to overpower a Hungarian team short on experience.

"We were lucky to get one point," said Norway's manager Egil Olsen. "Hungary surprised us in the first half. They played better than I've seen them before and we were lucky not to concede more goals."

Olsen was more satisfied with the result than Hungarian coach Janos Csank, who before the match had indicated he would be satisfied with a draw but after 90 minutes felt his team should have taken all three points.
"Based on the picture of the first half, we should have won," he said. "
Norway could have gone ahead as early as the first minute when Tore Flo, put through by Stig Inge Bjorneby, side-footed past the right-hand post with only goalkeeper Gabor Babos to beat.
Norbert Nagy also wasted an opportunity for Hungary before Petter Rudi nudged Norway in front after Babos could only palm out a long free kick by Henning Berg to Rudi. He volleyed in the rebound.

Hungary came back strongly and equalised through Zoltan Kovacs. He latched on to a delicate chip over the Norwegian defence by Hungary's man of the match, defender Emil Lorincz, to shoot powerfully past Frode Grodaas.

Hungary had several more chances in an exciting first half in which the Norwegian midfield ceded ground to the Hungarians, with Tamas Sandor and little winger Tibor Dombi tormenting a nervous Norway defence.

The frenetic pace subsided in the second half, although Frank Strandl's snap shot on the turn in the 56th minute whistled past Babos's post and Rudi brought out a fine double save from the Hungarian goalkeeper when he shot from 20 metres and followed up on the rebound.
For Hungary, Kovacs could have had a second when he overpowered Alf-Inge Haaland 40 metres out and darted forward to shoot straight at Grodaas.
The result kept both teams in the running for World Cup qualification, Norway maintaining their four-point lead in the group and Hungary moving ahead of Switzerland into joint second place.
